summary: 1 official and 1 generated header block(s) that correspond, grouped by address

answer.why_different: The generated document appears to have used a generic TS 28.532 service identity instead of the specific Performance Threshold Monitoring MnS identity, and it uses an older document version. It also adds generator provenance as an OpenAPI specification extension.
answer.spec_3gpp: The 3GPP evidence identifies the relevant service as the performance threshold monitoring service and defines performance-threshold notification data, supporting the specific Performance Threshold Monitoring identity. The supplied evidence does not establish whether 18.1.0 or 18.0.0 is the correct document version.
answer.openapi: The Info Object requires a title and version and permits an application description. Specification extensions beginning with `x-` are allowed, so the generated `x-openapi-generator` block is structurally valid OpenAPI 3.0 metadata.
answer.clearer_why: The official title and description identify the specific Performance Threshold Monitoring MnS, whereas the generated text describes the broader and less precise Generic management services document. The generator metadata is informative but does not compensate for the incorrect service identity.

citations.quote: title | `string` | **REQUIRED**. The title of the application.
The extensions properties are implemented as patterned fields that are always prefixed by `"x-"`.

differences.reason: The generated title changes the API identity from the specific Performance Threshold Monitoring MnS to Generic management services. This conflicts with the 3GPP evidence naming the relevant service the “Performance threshold monitoring service” (S3) and with the official context title (C1).

The version is a different value, and the OpenAPI reference confirms that it identifies the OpenAPI document, but the supplied 3GPP evidence does not determine whether 18.1.0 or 18.0.0 is correct. Therefore the meaning changes and the evidence does not decide between them (O2, C1, C2).

The generated description repeats the incorrect generic service identity and loses the specific Performance Threshold Monitoring MnS description. The 3GPP evidence identifies the service as performance threshold monitoring (S3), while the two description lines visibly differ in that identity (C1, C2).

The generated side adds useful provenance metadata, and OpenAPI 3.0 explicitly permits `x-` specification extensions with arbitrary valid values. It therefore adds information without invalidating the Info Object (O9, C2).

### Versions

The OpenAPI Specification is versioned using [Semantic Versioning 2.0.0](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html) (semver) and follows the semver specification.

The `major`.`minor` portion of the semver (for example `3.0`) SHALL designate the OAS feature set. Typically, *`.patch`* versions address errors in this document, not the feature set. Tooling which supports OAS 3.0 SHOULD be compatible with all OAS 3.0.\* versions. The patch version SHOULD NOT be considered by tooling, making no distinction between `3.0.0` and `3.0.1` for example.

Subsequent minor version releases of the OpenAPI Specification (incrementing the `minor` version number) SHOULD NOT interfere with tooling developed to a lower minor version and same major version.  Thus a hypothetical `3.1.0` specification SHOULD be usable with tooling designed for `3.0.0`.

An OpenAPI document compatible with OAS 3.\*.\* contains a required [`openapi`](#oasVersion) field which designates the semantic version of the OAS that it uses. (OAS 2.0 documents contain a top-level version field named [`swagger`](https://github.com/OAI/OpenAPI-Specification/blob/master/versions/2.0.md#swaggerObject) and value `"2.0"`.)
